key_insight: A CFD-based thermal simulation can accurately predict hot gas flow, surface heating, and melt-layer formation in serial hot gas welding of polypropylene.
engineering_relevance: This enables simulation-assisted design of hot gas tools and seam geometries, reducing trial-and-error experimentation and improving weld quality control.
method: Built a CFD model in ANSYS Fluent 2025 R2 for hot gas flow and transient heat transfer.
Used simulated temperature fields to derive melt-layer thickness and distribution in PP.
Validated against infrared thermography, high-pressure joining tests, and transmitted-light microscopy.
evidence_signal: Simulation matched experiments well, with surface temperature deviations below 10% and close agreement in melt-layer profiles and thickness.
watch_item: The study is demonstrated on polypropylene and one process setup, so broader transferability to other polymers, geometries, or tool designs still needs validation.
paper_title: Numerical and experimental analysis of melt layer formation in serial hot gas welding
